main_title: The Flight of the Condor and the Eagle
main_sub: Gnosis allows us to free ourselves from the material plane
header_desc: The meeting of the Condor and the Eagle symbolizes the ultimate union between science and spirituality, allowing us to understand that human consciousness is part of the Universe. It is precisely the Primordial Consciousness that has the mission of revealing to us that each cerebral hemisphere is linked to a different plane of the cosmos: while the material plane belongs to the psyche, the spiritual plane corresponds to the pneuma.
left_title: The Return of Sophia: From the Prison of Yaldabaoth 🧠 to the Kingdom of the ONE ❤️
left_body: What Christian tradition defines as the rapture is, in essence, a spiritual awakening known as the Return to Divine Unity. The Gnostic gospels, written nearly two thousand years ago, hold the key to one of the greatest enigmas of modern physics: quantum gravity. The EGO has mass and creates the tempo-material illusion of the psyche 🧠; to counter it, the cosmos offers us a Universal Consciousness, timeless and a-spatial —the ONE— which allows us to return to the divine timelessness of the pneuma ❤️.
universe_light_text: Understanding that death is not an absolute end, but a transformation, frees us from ignorance. In the right hemisphere —our pneuma— resides the a-temporal and divine plane, the high-frequency spiritual plane | 999⟩ is the origin of the cosmos where the Invisible Father dwells. There lies the land of union and freedom (The Great Homeland).
center_text: The Kingdom of God is within you (Gospel of Thomas, logion 3): Human consciousness manifests through two fundamental states: the spiritual |ONE⟩ —represented by Pistis Sophia and associated with the right hemisphere ❤️—, and the physical |EGO⟩ —represented by the Demiurge Yaldabaoth and associated with the left hemisphere 🧠—. This shows us that we possess a free will of perception, which can be mathematically formalized as an inner product ⟨ONE ❤️|EGO 🧠⟩.
universe_mat_text: The human body is composed of carbon-12 (6p^+, 6e^-, 6n^0). In the left hemisphere lies the temporal and material plane, the low-frequency physical plane | 666⟩ the end of the cosmos where Yaldabaoth resides. There is a place where: <q>war is peace, freedom is slavery, and ignorance is strength</q> (1984).
final_quote: When the Eagle of the North and the Condor of the South fly together in the same sky, Mother Earth will awaken and all of humanity will heal.
p2_sub: Condor and Eagle: The flight of science and spirituality
cap1_title: Chapter 1: The Prophecy of the Condor and the Eagle { footnotesize color{golddark}(00:10 -- 01:07)}
cap1_desc: Premise and framework for integration: the reconciliation between the intuitive wisdom of the South (the heart, ancestral knowledge, and spirit) and the technological development of the North (reason, science, and mind). The call for balance to initiate evolutionary awakening and transcend the state of duality.
cap2_title: Chapter 2: Quantum Gravity and Temporal Illusion { footnotesize color{golddark}(01:13 -- 02:42)}
cap2_desc: The fundamental clash of theoretical physics: General Relativity versus Quantum Mechanics. Why Newton's and Maxwell's laws do not distinguish between past and future, the breakdown of Einstein's simultaneity and the dissolution of linear time as a neural reconstruction of memory.
cap3_title: Chapter 3: Consciousness and Space-Time { footnotesize color{golddark}(02:47 -- 05:19)}
cap3_desc: The conceptual assembly Faggin--Segarra: the body as a vehicle operated by a conscious quantum field outside of space-time, where qualia reside. Consciousness does not arise from the brain but precedes it, converging with the First Consciousness and the Intelligent Designer free from time and space.
cap4_title: Chapter 4: Gnosis and Material Illusion { footnotesize color{golddark}(05:27 -- 08:39)}
cap4_desc: The finding of Nag Hammadi (1945) and the Coptic codices: the material cosmos conceived not as a home, but as a prison of the soul. The teaching of the Gospel of Thomas (Logion 3): Jesus did not come to establish a religion of dogmas, but to free the inner spark from the prison of the Demiurge through remembrance (gnosis).
cap5_title: Chapter 5: The Kingdom of Light and the Prison of the Demiurge { footnotesize color{golddark}(08:43 -- 10:16)}
cap5_desc: The Demiurge Yaldabaoth —also known as the great architect of matter— is the creator of the sensible world, an egocentric god ignorant of true divinity. On the other hand, Sophia lies captive in the density of matter, awaiting the spark of awakening.
cap6_title: Chapter 6: The Dajjal and the Universal Hemispheres { footnotesize color{golddark}(10:23 -- 14:38)}
cap6_desc: Comparative eschatology and perceptual distortion: the figure of the Dajjal and the optical illusion of the inverted paradise (the river and the fire). The mechanism of Orwellian doublethink (1984) as a cognitive prison of the ego, versus the revolutionary message of Jesus that dismantles the imperial slavery system.
cap7_title: Chapter 7: Reflections on Our Place in the Cosmos { footnotesize color{golddark}(14:40 -- 16:30)}
cap7_desc: The end, the great paradox reduces to this: in the vastness of the cosmos —with its more than two trillion galaxies— it is there that the phrase of Jesus resonates most strongly: 'The Father and I are one.' Could this have had a hidden message about the deep bond between humanity and the cosmos?
sagan_quote: <q>The idea that God is a white man, larger than normal, with a flowing beard, sitting in heaven and counting the fall of every sparrow, is ridiculous. But if by God one understands the set of physical laws that govern the universe, then such a God clearly exists. However, this God is emotionally unsatisfying... it doesn’t make much sense to pray to the law of gravity</q>
